$comment: Rule catalog — source control safety. Standard 46. Committed secrets route to security.no-secrets-in-artifacts (Standard 16 R2) rather than being duplicated here.

rules.title: Environment files are not committed
rules.description: No dotenv-style environment file is tracked. Example, template, sample, and vault variants are permitted, since they carry placeholders rather than values.
rules.rationale: An environment file is where a project puts the values it must not publish, so a tracked file of that name is the finding and no content scan is needed to establish it.
rules.remediation: Remove it from tracking with `git rm --cached`, add it to .gitignore, rotate anything it contained, and commit an example variant in its place.
rules.$assuranceNote: Filename to find the candidates, then the repository index to decide, through the ADR 0008 seam. The detector never reads the contents and does not need to: the question is whether a file of that name is tracked, not what is in it. A gitignored .env on a developer's machine is therefore not a finding, and where the index cannot be read the rule reports not-evaluated rather than passing or failing — there is no working-tree fallback, by ADR 0011's constraint against minting a second answer to a question this seam exists to answer once. Partial rather than full because it recognises dotenv-shaped names and their permitted example/template/sample/vault variants, so a project keeping its values in a file named nothing like an environment file is outside what this can see. security.no-secrets-in-artifacts excludes these files by design so that one defect produces one finding.

rules.title: Build output is not committed unnecessarily
rules.description: Build output and local editor state are not tracked. Lockfiles, golden files, generated code a build cannot reproduce, and vendored dependencies recorded in a decision record are deliberate and are not this rule's subject.
rules.rationale: Recommended rather than forbidden because the necessary cases are common enough that a prohibition would be excepted more often than it fired, which teaches a team to except rules by reflex.
rules.remediation: Untrack the artifact and add it to .gitignore, or record why it is committed in a decision record.
rules.$assuranceNote: Distinguishing accidental build output from a deliberate lockfile is a judgement about intent, not a property of the path.

rules.title: Shared history is not rewritten without justification
rules.description: History on a shared branch is not rewritten, and meaningful history is not deleted to simplify an implementation. Purging a leaked secret is the exception, and it expires with the operation.
rules.rationale: A force-push to a shared branch invalidates every other clone of it, and a deleted commit takes its evidence with it.
rules.remediation: Revert forward rather than rewriting. Where a purge is genuinely required, record the justification, the approval, and the notice sent to everyone holding a clone.
rules.$assuranceNote: Recorded blind spot: detecting a rewrite requires comparing history against a previous observation of the same history, which a single repository snapshot does not contain.
